wa_crisis_wall.blurb: Crisis Wall is a small granite face within McLellan Rocks, a cluster of low domes and corridors set among ponderosa pine on the south side of the Spokane River, west of Spokane. Nearly everything here is bolted: sixteen sport lines and a single trad route. The grades spread evenly from easy 5.6 up through the low 5.12s, with a few routes in each band, so a mixed group can find something. Climbs face east and nearby trees add shade. The walk in is short, a few minutes past the pond. It was one of the earliest walls at McLellan to get bolts, and it makes a decent stop between neighbouring walls.

wa_m_m_wall.blurb: M & M Wall is a short, steep basalt cliff in Echo Basin, down the coulee from Sunshine Wall near Vantage. The rock is red columnar basalt, roughly forty feet tall, and the climbing is technical and crimpy, with stemming, body tension and some power. Most of the seventeen lines are sport, backed by five trad routes. Grades cluster heavily in the 5.11 range, with a few easier and one 5.12, so it suits climbers already comfortable in that territory. Expect bolts that are spaced a little farther than usual. The wall was where hard sport climbing took hold in the coulee in the mid-1990s, and it still draws steady interest.
wa_m_m_wall.approach: From the main lot, go up to the mesa and down the first gully, then continue to Sunshine Wall's east corner. Take the trail heading downhill, bearing left of Fat Man Wall, and follow its switchbacks a little further down to the base.

wa_bill_s_wall.blurb: Bill's Wall is a basalt wall at the quiet far end of Sunshine Wall in Echo Basin, near Vantage, sitting between the Tilted Pillars and Tomato Wall. Most of its seventeen routes are traditional lines that see few ascents; two are bolted. Grades run from 5.7 up to 5.11, with the bulk in the 5.9 to 5.10 range, making it a reasonable choice for trad leaders warming into the grade. The surrounding far-end walls offer relief from both wind and hot sun at different times of day, so it can be a useful fallback when the main crags are blasted. Expect a walk down a gully to reach it.

yt_1_3_bolt_wonderland.blurb: 3 Bolt Wonderland is a short limestone sport crag among the Roadside Crags on the road out of Whitehorse toward Atlin, close to Mount White. It holds seventeen bolted routes, mostly brief but well regarded. The grades are concentrated around 5.10, with ten routes there, and a handful of easier lines from about 5.6 to 5.8, which makes it a handy place to warm up before something harder. The setting is sunny and open, and by Yukon standards it can see a crowd. Pull-out parking sits beside the road, so the walk to the base is trivial.
